aspects.says: The JVM checks a sealed supertype again when it loads a subclass and throws IncompatibleClassChangeError for one that is unlisted or in another module.
basis: section:Permitted Subclasses Live in the Sealed Type's Module, or in Its Package When There Is No Module
aspects.reason: the check shows only when class files are moved between modules after compiling, which a practice built as one Maven project cannot do

aspects.says: A permitted subclass must declare final, sealed or non-sealed; javac has no default and reports the subclass that declares none.
basis: section:Every Permitted Subclass Says Whether the Hierarchy Goes On: final, sealed or non-sealed

aspects.says: A non-sealed subclass or subinterface lets any class extend it, so the set of classes below a sealed root is no longer known.
basis: section:non-sealed Reopens One Branch, and Subtypes Nobody Listed Arrive Through Its Case

aspects.says: A switch over the sealed root stays exhaustive with a case for the non-sealed type, and every unknown subtype of it runs that case, with no compile error and no MatchException.
basis: section:non-sealed Reopens One Branch, and Subtypes Nobody Listed Arrive Through Its Case

aspects.says: A record is implicitly final, and an enum is implicitly final, or sealed when a constant has a body, so neither needs a modifier; a permitted interface can't be final.
basis: section:Records and Enums Are Already final, or sealed
aspects.reason: the compiler enforces which modifiers records, enums and interfaces take, so no wrong solution compiles for a test to catch

aspects.says: Permitted subclasses must be in the sealed type's named module, or in its package when it is in the unnamed module.
basis: section:Permitted Subclasses Live in the Sealed Type's Module, or in Its Package When There Is No Module

aspects.says: A sealed subclass keeps the hierarchy closed below it: only its own permitted subclasses can extend it.
basis: section:Every Permitted Subclass Says Whether the Hierarchy Goes On: final, sealed or non-sealed
section:A sealed Subclass Keeps the Set Closed, but a Switch Needs a Case for It Unless It Is Abstract

aspects.says: A sealed subclass that is not abstract has instances of its own, so covering its permitted subclasses does not cover it.
basis: section:A sealed Subclass Keeps the Set Closed, but a Switch Needs a Case for It Unless It Is Abstract

aspects.says: A switch over the root covers a sealed subclass through its permitted subclasses only when it is abstract or an interface; otherwise the switch needs a case for it.
basis: section:A sealed Subclass Keeps the Set Closed, but a Switch Needs a Case for It Unless It Is Abstract
